recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a dead-man's-switch heartbeat: nightly-sync pings a URL when it succeeds, and a monitor alerts the user if no ping arrives by about 03:30. The monitor can be a self-hosted healthchecks container on the Synology or a free hosted service.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to stop missing silent failures of nightly-sync without reading logs — the actual need is "tell me when the job doesn't finish," not "store all logs centrally."
labels.Deleted: A central Docker log stack (Loki/Grafana/ELK-style) on the Synology — it wouldn't have caught last week's failure either, since the crash happened before the email step ever wrote anything worth logging, and you said you won't read logs anyway.
labels.Bottleneck: nightly-sync only speaks at the end (the summary email); when it dies at startup it says nothing, so the single fix is making silence itself the alert.
labels.Checked myself: From what you told me — cron on edna at 03:00, email only on completion, last failure was an expired token at startup, four nights unnoticed, nothing else alerts today.

note: It is one alert, but the reply offers a self-hosted healthchecks Docker container on the Synology as an acceptable choice, so it partly recommends the user's framed stack and counts as LARGER.
